name: firstbell-absence-calls
title: n8n school-absence call wave, in each family's language
description: Inactive-by-default n8n workflow that calls the families whose absence notification went unanswered, each in that family's own language, and keeps three outcomes apart: a usable answer, a conversation that produced nothing, and nobody reached. Ships with a dry run that places no calls.

entrypoints.name: Call the families whose absence is still unexplained, in their own language

side_effects: Creates outbound phone calls only after CALL_E_API_KEY is configured, the shipped placeholder numbers are replaced, and dryRun is set to false.
Deactivation stops new runs but does not cancel accepted calls. Calls v2 permits cancellation only before provider submission; this template does not send cancellation requests.
safety: Imports inactive and runs from its Manual Trigger. The schedule node ships disabled.
dryRun is true on import, so the first end-to-end run places no calls and needs no API key.
Refuses to dial the shipped placeholder numbers, which use the +91 555 range that cannot be assigned to a subscriber.
Validates every destination number as E.164 before the wave starts, rather than failing halfway through it.
Consent is never inferred. A row without recorded consent is refused rather than defaulted, and is reported as skipped rather than counted among the failures, because no call was placed.
Masks phone numbers in every displayed output, so a family's number does not reach an execution log.
Discloses in the first three sentences of the call that the caller is an AI assistant and that a member of staff can be requested at any time.
Caps concurrency at three and the wait across one row's fallback numbers at four minutes.

Derives one Idempotency-Key per student, absence date and number index. Recovery must preserve the original row, request and number order. Only confirmed no-answer or busy permits the next authorized number.
credentials: CALL-E API key read from $env.CALL_E_API_KEY in a self-hosted n8n Code node. Live use requires environment access enabled (N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false); dry run never reads environment values. No key is stored in workflow data or exports.

verification.unit_tests: node --test examples/classify.test.mjs examples/workflow-shape.test.mjs, 35 passing on node 26.8.2. Name both files: `node --test examples/` resolves the directory as a module on this version and fails before it reads a test. The 27 classifier tests cover the three-outcome rule, the two shapes of an unusable answer, the refusal to borrow a task-level result on fan-out, number masking, the attempt ledger, the subset of the result schema this recipe re-validates, and the safeguarding axis: that it fails closed on anything but an explicit yes, that it never becomes a fourth resolution, that it attaches to an answer that learned nothing as readily as to one that did, that an escalated call is not counted as closed, that an escalated call which was never resolved cannot push the closed count below zero, and that it sorts to the top of the queue. The 8 shape tests are described under structure_validated.
verification.generated: examples/absence-wave.workflow.json is generated by examples/build-workflow.mjs, which inlines the tested classifier. Regeneration is byte-identical and one test fails if the workflow and the tested module drift apart.
verification.rule_validated: The safeguarding rule was broken five ways and the suite caught each one: the rule never escalating, escalating on a missing field but not on an explicit no, an escalated call no longer needing a human, escalated attempts counted as work saved, and the queue no longer sorting safeguarding first. Killed by 3, 3, 2, 2 and 2 tests. Read those counts with one caveat: the test asserting that the workflow embeds exactly the code these tests ran fires for any edit to classify.mjs, so it is one of the killers in every row and each of the twos is one rule test plus that structural one. A rule nobody has watched fail has not been shown to do anything.
verification.structure_validated: examples/workflow-shape.test.mjs asserts the invariants n8n needs to load a workflow: the two collections it reads, the five fields each node is drawn from, unique names and ids, no connection naming a node that is absent, at least one trigger, no orphan node, no credential baked into the file, and that the shipped dry run closes at least one record, escalates exactly one, and puts the escalated row first in the queue. Each of the five was checked by breaking the workflow that way and confirming the suite goes red: a renamed node with a stale connection, a duplicate name, a missing position, every trigger removed, and a live key inlined in a parameter. All five were caught, and the file was restored byte-identical. The dry-run check was measured the same way, twice. Removing parent_confirmed_aware from the shipped shapes, which is the state this plugin actually shipped in for a day, fails it: 26 of 26 passed while the demo closed nothing, because nothing else in either suite reads the shapes. Changing the resolution rate the plugin README publishes for that run, from 40 percent to 60, fails it too, because the test reads the figure out of the README rather than holding its own copy of it.
verification.not_verified: No production school register, real family calls, hosted schedule or existing online instance was switched. Local import and dry run do not establish school deployment acceptance.
verification.calls_v2: node --test examples/workflow-v2.test.mjs executes the exported Code nodes with fake HTTP and clock seams, covering result readiness, fallback keys, uncertain requests, API IDs, safeguarding and dry-run behavior.
verification.n8n_import: Imported into isolated n8n 2.44.6 on 2026-10-25 and executed by CLI without a CALL-E key. All six synthetic rows completed: five attempted, one skipped, two closed, one safeguarding entry first, resolution rate 40 percent. Workflow inactive; schedule disabled.
verification.live_replay: The original authorized hotline request and idempotency key were replayed through the actual n8n Code node with $env access enabled. The API returned the same completed Call ID; workflow execution succeeded without a replacement Call.
